name: Griffon Corporation
reason: Garage-door (Clopay) and lawn/garden tools holding company whose EBIT margin is at a 10y high of 17.8% vs a 9.4% average with EPS at 1.0x its 10y peak, 10y avg ROIC only 1.9% and a 173% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap - housing/repair-cyclical earnings at peak with no clear moat.

name: Graham Holdings Co.
reason: Shareholder-friendly conglomerate (Kaplan, TV stations, home infusion, auto dealers, manufacturing) with net cash and shares shrinking 2.7%/yr, but EPS swings wildly ($13.79 to $163.40 on investment gains) and 5.1% EBIT margin across unrelated businesses cannot be forecast 5-10 years out.

name: Liberty Capital Corporation
reason: Recently spun Alaska telecom (GCI) with only three years of standalone EPS ending in a $-7.76 GAAP loss, dependence on federal rural subsidy programmes and an LTM 14.9% FCF yield on CFO-capex that is not yet proven recurring (10y FCF conversion 0.14).

name: Global Net Lease Inc
reason: Externally-born net-lease REIT with FFO/share falling from $2.46 to $0.99 (5y CAGR -11.2%), share count up 14.4%/yr and net debt/EBITDA 6.6x - value-destructive, over-levered and office-exposed.

name: Generac Holdings Inc.
reason: Dominant US home-standby generator brand, but demand is driven by unforecastable outage/storm events, EPS sits at 0.66x its 2021 peak with margin at the 18th percentile, and the data-center/energy-tech pivot plus a 61% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap make the 5-10 year path unclear.

name: Genuine Parts Company
reason: Solid NAPA/Motion distributor but 10y EPS CAGR only 4.8% with EBIT margin down to 5.1% (9th percentile), net debt/EBITDA 3.65x, a 299% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap and share loss to AutoZone/O'Reilly - ordinary, not special.

name: Green Thumb Industries Inc.
reason: Leading US multi-state cannabis operator with 14.5% FCF yield and low leverage, but federal illegality makes rescheduling/banking/taxation a binary regulatory outcome, prices are deflating and share count rose 122%/yr historically.

name: Getty Realty Corp.
reason: Convenience/gas-station net-lease REIT with near-flat AFFO/share (10y CAGR 1.4%), shares up 5.4%/yr, net debt/EBITDA 5.6x and long-run EV risk to fuel-station tenants - stable but no route to 7% per-share growth.

name: Hasbro, Inc.
reason: Wizards of the Coast (Magic, Monopoly Go) is a valuable IP franchise, but EPS is at its 10y peak with EBIT margin at a 22.5% record vs a 14.1% average, the toy business is shrinking and hit-driven digital licensing plus 3.1% avg ROIC (eOne write-downs) make the future hard to forecast.

name: Healthcare Services Group, Inc.
reason: Housekeeping/dietary outsourcer to nursing homes whose EBIT margin has collapsed to 0.5% (from 7.5%), 10y EPS CAGR 1.6%, and whose customers' solvency depends on Medicaid/Medicare reimbursement - net cash but no specialness.

name: Hecla Mining Company
reason: Silver/gold miner whose earnings are set by metal prices: EPS $0.44 is at its 10y max with EBIT margin at a record 37.5% vs 8.2% average and 10y avg ROIC 0.6%, shares up 5.8%/yr - commodity peak.

name: Houlihan Lokey, Inc.
reason: High-quality mid-market advisory franchise (EPS CAGR 17.9%, ROIC 18.5%, net cash) with a counter-cyclical restructuring hedge, but revenue is still set by M&A/capital-markets activity and EPS is at 1.0x its 10y peak.

name: Harley-Davidson, Inc.
reason: Iconic brand in structural decline - revenue 10y CAGR -2.9%, EPS CAGR -2.8%, EBIT margin down to 5.4% (18th percentile) on an ageing rider base, with a captive consumer-credit arm adding credit-cycle risk.

name: HealthEquity, Inc.
reason: Leading HSA custodian with secular account growth (rev CAGR 26%), but earnings are heavily driven by yields earned on custodial cash (interest-rate dependent), growth was bought (acquisitions 2.8x FCF, shares up 4%/yr) and a 167% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap obscures true economics.

name: Harrow, Inc.
reason: Small ophthalmic pharma still loss-making on GAAP (EPS $-0.14 in 2025, never consistently profitable), net debt/EBITDA 3.1x, shares up 14.4%/yr and product/reimbursement risk - fails durability and balance-sheet tests.

name: Host Hotels & Resorts, Inc.
reason: Lodging REIT whose FFO is set by the travel/economic cycle (FFO $-0.17 in 2020, now at 10y peak $2.07) with 10y FFO CAGR 3.0% and consensus implying decline - cyclical and ordinary.

name: Hershey Company
reason: Dominant US chocolate franchise (Hershey's, Reese's) with 10y avg ROIC 23% and 8/10 years of >=7% EPS growth to 2023; 2025 EPS fell 33% on record cocoa costs (margin 12.6% vs 20.7% avg) and recovery toward ~$9.6+ NTM plus pricing power gives a route to >=7%/yr - cocoa and GLP-1 risks need testing in deep dive.

name: Hub Group, Inc.
reason: Asset-light intermodal/logistics broker tied to the freight cycle: EPS $1.54 is 0.29x its 2022 peak, EBIT margin 3.6%, and the 12.2% NTM FCF yield reflects a trough-capex cycle rather than a special business.

name: Huntsman Corporation
reason: Cyclical MDI/polyurethanes chemical producer with GAAP losses (EPS $-0.70), EBIT margin -0.7%, net debt/EBITDA 7.95x and revenue shrinking 5.8%/yr - commodity chemical with stretched balance sheet.

name: Huron Consulting Group Inc.
reason: Healthcare/education consultancy with EPS at its 10y high ($7.83) and margin at the 82nd percentile after a run-up, but 10y avg ROIC only 3.6% and no durable moat in project-based consulting - good execution, not special.
